newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-HUSSAIN HITS DOUBLE CENTURY AS ENGLAND DOMINATE.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-HUSSAIN HITS DOUBLE CENTURY AS ENGLAND DOMINATE.

text.p: Nasser Hussain struck a career-best 207 on Friday to strengthen England's grip on the first Ashes test against Australia on the second day at Edgbaston.
Hussain was dismissed just before tea, as England moved to 418 for six at the end of the second session for an overall lead of 300.
The middle order batsman's innings included 38 fours and featured some brilliant strokes through the covers. He faced 336 balls and batted for seven hours 20 minutes.
Hussain edged Shane Warne to wicketkeeper Ian Healy, giving the leg-spinner his first wicket of the series with the first ball of his 29th over.
But Warne, who has proved Australia's match-winner against England on several occasions this decade, proved largely ineffective, costing more than 100 runs.
Graham Thorpe also made his highest test score, before falling in the second over after lunch, pulling Glenn McGrath from outside the off-stump to give Michael Bevan an easy catch at mid-on.
He had made 138 from 245 balls in just under five hours, with 19 fours.
Thorpe's partnership with Hussain was worth 288, beating the previous best fourth-wicket stand for England in an Ashes match by 66 runs.
Three overs later, John Crawley, having already edged Mike Kasprowicz just short of second slip, touched another ball from the same bowler to Healy.
Crawley made only one, but Australia's hopes of quickly wrapping up the innings were frustrated by Hussain and Mark Ealham, who was 20 not out at tea.

McGrath and Kasprowicz were by far the best of the depleted attack available to skipper Mark Taylor. Steve Waugh, forced to bowl a long spell because of injuries to Jason Gillespie and Greg Blewett, and Warne both tightened up in the second session after poor spells in the morning.
